posts.t:
Harsh

You would have to excuse me, but i disagree with you. mainly because thru my experience, the market obey levels with ever surprising precision. I gave a lot of thinking about how come a vast and dynamic market that represent masses of conflicting opinions / methods / interpretations and motivations, can be end up at a very accurate pin point level. My explanation for this (its only my own unproven theory), is that the players at the market are pushing price in directions, but the price reaction and turning happen when price hit stacks of remaining SD orders.

Therefore, dissecting the levels to understand the order flow status at a level can be a powerful trading tool.

Hi Gian This is just my understanding on what I think Ben Hur is trying to explain and I hope he will correct me if I am wrong. The first chart below is is the supply zone of a weekly RBD and I have marked a bar that i am trying to explain with an arrow and have extended it across.

The second chart is a daily chart with 5 candle highlighted in green which makes up the 1 candle on the weekly. nothing major can be seen.

the third chart is a 4 hr chart with 20 candles which makes up the 1 weekly candle. there seems to be some activity

the fourth chart chart is the 1 hr and in here you can see and I have marked it with an arrow where the sellers overcame the buyers. As price shot off so quickly there will still be some unfilled orders in here

I have marked on the next chart the place where price shot off with a green line.

If we now go back to the weekly chart you will that price went up to the green line that I placed on the i hr chart and shot back down again.

I sincerely hope my understanding is correct and anyone please correct me if am wrong. Hang in there Gian it will all become clear just keep reading and trying to learn as there are some wonderful and very helpful people here. Hope this helps. Tino

I just want to clarify some terminology, before I start on this assignment.

What is the relationship with or difference between an engulf and a DBR RBD? From one perspective an engulf could be a part of a DBR.

Is an engulf just a dip in price or does it require an actual engulfing candle (which would affectively limit an engulf to a dip based on two candles). If it requires an engulfing candle, then an engulf could affectively be a peak and not just a dip. From what I remember, on the 5 or so videos I've watched, the reference to an engulf has only been a dip.

Yes...... I'm anal..... sorry.
posts.fa:
فقط می‌خوام چند اصطلاح رو روشن کنم، قبل از اینکه شروع کنم به این تمرین.

رابطه یا تفاوت اینگالف با DBR و RBD چیه؟ از یک زاویه، اینگالف می‌تونه بخشی از یک DBR باشه.

آیا اینغالف فقط یک فرو رفتن قیمته یا به یک کندلِ واقعاً اینغالف‌کننده نیاز داره (که عملاً اینغالف رو به یک فرو رفتن بر اساس دو کندل محدود می‌کنه)؟ اگه به کندلِ واقعاً اینغالف‌کننده نیاز داشته باشه، پس اینغالف عملاً می‌تونه یک قله باشه و نه فقط یک فرو رفتن. از چیزی که یادم می‌آد، در حدود 5 ویدئویی که دیدم، اشاره به اینغالف فقط به‌صورت یک فرو رفتن بوده.

بله… وسواسی‌ام… ببخشید.

posts.t:
Hi Harry. Thanks for your reply.

What I am getting from your last is that engulfing applies to both RBDs and a flag limits.

Which is fair, if I'm correct.

You mentioned an "RBD engulfing a previous one." That part did not make complete sense. And if there is something already written about this somewhere, don't waste your time on me. But I haven't seen anything as of yet.

Also, is it me or is a RBR and a DBD (on higher timeframes especially) the same or very similar to a flag limit?

Are these just interchangeable terms?

RBD = engulf DBR = engulf FL = RBR or DBD

Am I correct? Terminology is very important to me as you can see.

EDIT ----From the Supply and Demand page

"supply/demand are often reactions to the Flag Limit (a RBD or DBR after a break of a high or low)."

This makes things a little clearer, but I still want to be clear on what is definitely interchangeable and what is not.

EDIT ---

from this page: readthemarket.com/index.php/price-reading "In LTF, does price react violently to the first decision point? Does it quickly engulf the nearest S/D? (good sign)"

This bolded question leads me to believe an engulf can be both up or down.
posts.fa:
سلام Harry. ممنون از جوابت.

چیزی که از حرف آخرت برداشت می‌کنم اینه که اینگالف هم به RBD‌ها و هم به FL‌ها مربوط می‌شه.

که منصفانه‌ست، اگه درست فهمیده باشم.

گفتی «یک RBD که RBD قبلی رو اینگالف می‌کنه». اون بخش کاملاً برام روشن نشد. و اگه جایی دربارهٔ این موضوع نوشته شده، وقتت رو با من هدر نده. ولی من تا حالا چیزی ندیدم.

همچنین، آیا فقط نظر منه یا RBR و DBD (خصوصاً در تایم‌فریم‌های بالاتر) همون FL یا خیلی شبیهش هستن؟

آیا این‌ها فقط اصطلاحات قابل‌جایگزینی هستن؟

RBD = اینگالف، DBR = اینگالف، FL = RBR یا DBD

درست می‌گم؟ همون‌طور که می‌بینی اصطلاحات برای من خیلی مهم‌اند.

ویرایش ----از صفحهٔ عرضه و تقاضا

«عرضه/تقاضا اغلب واکنش‌هایی به FL هستند (یک RBD یا DBR بعد از شکست یک سقف یا کف).»

این یه‌کم روشن‌ترش می‌کنه، ولی هنوز می‌خوام دقیق بدونم چی قطعاً قابل‌جایگزینیه و چی نه.

ویرایش ---

از این صفحه: readthemarket.com/index.php/price-reading «در LTF، آیا قیمت به اولین نقطهٔ تصمیم واکنش شدید نشون می‌ده؟ آیا سریع نزدیک‌ترین S/D رو اینگالف می‌کنه؟ (نشانهٔ خوب)»

این سؤال بولدشده من رو به این باور می‌رسونه که اینگالف می‌تونه هم بالا باشه هم پایین.
